Analysis workflow

Common preprocessing

All analysis modes begin by:

  1. reading Visiopharm object-level tables;

  2. constructing per-sample AnnData objects;

  3. applying user-defined rules for major cell types; and

  4. storing cell-level annotations and spatial/intensity information.

Execution then branches according to type_of_analysis.

Supervised branch

The supervised branch applies user-defined subtype rules, calculates cell-population counts and proportions, generates hierarchy information, and produces requested spatial plots.

Unsupervised branch

The unsupervised branch:

  1. creates cell-type proportion matrices;

  2. identifies binary protein marker patterns observed in the data;

  3. quantifies those patterns within selected major cell types;

  4. stores discovered phenotype labels/patterns in AnnData;

  5. optionally compares phenotypes between two sample groups; and

  6. optionally summarizes marker intensities within discovered phenotypes.

Full branch

Full mode runs the unsupervised branch first, converts discovered protein marker patterns into subtype definitions, and then invokes the supervised workflow.

Questions answered by each mode

Supervised

Which predefined phenotypes are present, how abundant are they, and how are they spatially distributed?

Unsupervised

Which marker combinations are observed within a selected parent population, how abundant are they, and do their proportions differ between groups?

Neither mode alone establishes biological lineage or causality.
